questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The length, breadth and thickness of a block are given by $l=12 \mathrm{~cm}, b=6 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $t=2.45 \mathrm{~cm}$. The volume of the block according to the idea of significant figures should be
questions.solution:
Using the relation for volume
$V=$ length \times  breadth \times  thickness
$\begin{aligned} & =12 \times 6 \times 2.45=176.4 \\ & =1.764 \times 10^2 \mathrm{~cm}^3\end{aligned}$
The minimum number of significant figures is 1 in breadth, hence the volume will contain only one significant figure.
Therefore, $V=2 \times 10^2 \mathrm{~cm}^3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensional formula for Young's modulus is
questions.solution:
The formula for the Young's modulus
$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\text { stress }}{\text { strain }}$
Dimensions of $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Y} & =\frac{\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}}{\mathrm{M}^0 \mathrm{~L}^0 \mathrm{~T}^0} \\ & =\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A police jeep is chasing with velocity of $45 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. A thief in another jeep moving with velocity $153 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. Police fires a bullet with muzzle velocity of $180 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The velocity it will strike the car of the thief is
questions.solution:
Effective speed of bullet is \(=\) Speed of bullet + Speed of police jeep
\(\begin{aligned}
& =18 \mathrm{om} / \mathrm{s}+45 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr} \\
& =180+45 \times \frac{5}{18} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
& =192.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}\)
Speed of theifs jeep \(=153 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}=42.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\)
Velocity of bullet with respect to theif's jeep \(=192.5-42.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\)
\(=150 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The maximum range of a gun on horizontal terrain is 16 km , if $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$. What must be the muzzle velocity of the shell?
questions.solution:
We know that in projection of the particle, for maximum range, $\theta=45^{\circ}$
Now maximum range
$\begin{aligned} & R=\frac{u^2 \sin 2 \theta}{g}=\frac{u^2 \sin 90^{\circ}}{g} \\ & u=\sqrt{R g} & ...(1) \end{aligned}$
Here : $R_{\max }=16 \mathrm{~km}=16 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~m}$,
$g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$
Now from eq. (1), we get
$u=\sqrt{16 \times 10^3 \times 10}=400 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Five particles of mass 2 kg are attached to the rim of a circular disc of radius 0.1 m and negligible mass. Moment of inertia of the system about the axis passing through the centre of the disc and perpendicular to its plane is
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of the given system that contains 5 particles each of mass $=2 \mathrm{~kg}$ on the rim of circular disc of radius 0.1 m and of negligible mass is given by
$=\text { MI of disc }+ \text { MI of particle }$
Since the mass of the disc is negligible therefore, MI of the system $=$ MI of particle
$=5 \times 2 \times(0.1)^2=0.1 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sphere of diameter 0.2 m and mass 2 kg is rolling on an inclined plane with velocity $v=0.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The kinetic energy of the sphere is
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of sphere while rolling on an inclined plane is given by
$E_K=\text { Translational kinetic energy }+ 	ext{ Rotational kinetic energy}\begin{aligned}= & \frac{1}{2} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} I \omega^2 \\ E_K= & \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times(0.5)^2+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{3} \times 2 \times(0.1)^2 \times\left(\frac{0.5}{0.1}\right)^2 \\ = & 0.25+0.17=0.42 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is kept at rest at the top of a sphere of diameter 42 m . When disturbed slightly, it slides down. At what height $h$ from the bottom, the particle will leave the sphere?
questions.solution: The condition of slipping by particle from top is given by $\cos \theta=2 / 3$ From the figure, $h=r \cos \theta=21 \times \frac{2}{3}=14 \mathrm{~m}$ Therefore, the required height at which the particle will leave the sphere is $=21+h=21+14=35 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Radius of orbit of satellite of earth is $R$. Its kinetic energy is proportional to
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy of the satellite
$\mathrm{KE}=\frac{1}{2} m v_0^2$ ...(1)
where $v_0=\sqrt{\frac{G M}{R}}$
Now putting the value of $v_0$ is eq. (1), we get
$\mathrm{KE}=\frac{1}{2} m\left(\sqrt{\frac{G M}{R}}\right)^2=\frac{1}{2} \frac{m G M}{R}$
Hence, $\mathrm{KE} \propto \frac{1}{R}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radius $R$ of the soap bubble is doubled under isothermal condition. If $T$ be the surface tension of soap bubble. The work done in doing so is given by
questions.solution:
Initial surface energy
$w_1=2 \times 4 \pi R^2 T=8 \pi R^2 T$
Final surface energy
$w_2=2 \times 4 \pi(2 R)^2 T=32 \pi R^2 T$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A tank is filled with water upto height $H$. When a hole is made at a distance $h$ below the level of water. What will be the horizontal range of water jet?
questions.solution: Applying Bernoullis' theorem, the velocity of water at point $v=\sqrt{2 g h}$ Time take on to reach point $C$ is $t$ So, $\quad H-h=\frac{1}{2} g t^2t=\sqrt{\frac{2(H-h)}{g}}$ ...(1) Now horizontal range $\begin{aligned} R & =v t \\ & =\sqrt{2 g h} \times \sqrt{\frac{2(H-h)}{g}}=2 \sqrt{(H-h) h}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A raft of wood of mass 120 kg floats in water. The weight that can be put on the raft to make it just sink, should be $\left(d_{\text {raft }}=600 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3\right)$
questions.solution:
Volume of raft is given by
$V=\frac{m}{d}=\frac{120}{600}=0.2 \mathrm{~m}^3$
If the raft is immersed fully in water.
Then weight of water displaced is $=V d_{\text {water }}=0.2 \times 10^3=200 \mathrm{~kg}$
Hence, the additional weight which is supported by raft
$=200 \mathrm{~kg}-120 \mathrm{~kg}=80 \mathrm{~kg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of specific heat $0.2 \mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{kg}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is heated through $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The percentage increase in its mass is
questions.solution:
Heat taken by the given body $=m c \Delta \theta$
{specific heat of body $=0.2 \mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{kg}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, final temperature of the body $\left.=100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right\}\begin{aligned} \Delta E & =m \times 0.2 \times 100=20 \mathrm{mkcal} \\ & =20 \mathrm{~m} \times 4.2 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
Now gain in mass is given by
$\Delta m=\frac{\Delta E}{C^2}\left(\because E=m c^2\right)=\frac{20 \mathrm{~m} \times 4.2 \times 10^3}{\left(3 \times 10^8\right)^2}$
Therefore, percentage increase in mass is given by
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\Delta m}{m} \times 100 \\ & =\frac{20 m \times 4.2 \times 10^3}{\left(3 \times 10^8\right)^2 \times m} \times 100 \\ & =9.3 \times 10^{-11} \%\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A steel scale measures the length of a copper wire as 80.0 cm, when both are at $20^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the calibration temperature for the scale. What would the scale read for the length of the rod when both are at $40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ?
Given: $\alpha$ for steel $=11 \times 10^{-6}$ per ${ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $\alpha$ for $\mathrm{Cu}=17 \times 10^{-6}$ per $^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
questions.solution:
Using the relation $l_t=l_0(1+\alpha t)\begin{aligned} & =1 \times\left[1+11 \times 10^{-6} \times\left(40^{\circ}-20^{\circ}\right)\right] \\ & =1.00022 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
Now length of copper rod at $40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\begin{aligned} R_t{ }^{\prime} & =l_0{ }^{\prime}\left(1+\alpha^{\prime} t\right) \\ & =80\left[1+17 \times 10^{-6}\left(40^{\circ}-20^{\circ}\right)\right] \\ & =80.0272 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
Now number of cms observed on the scale
$=\frac{80.0272}{1.00022}=80.0096$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The temperature of the black body increases from $T$ to $2 T$. The factor by which the rate of emission will increase, is?
questions.solution:
According to Stefan's law for radiated energy
$E \propto T^4$
Hence,
$\frac{E_1}{E_2}=\frac{T_1^4}{T_2^4}=\left(\frac{T}{2 T}\right)^4=\frac{1}{16}\therefore \quad E_2=16 E_1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A monoatomic gas supplied the heat $Q$ very slowly keeping the pressure constant. The work done by the gas will be
questions.solution:
For monoatomic gas at constant pressure
$\frac{\Delta U}{Q}=\frac{1}{3}$
or $\quad \Delta U=\frac{Q}{3}$
Now applying first law of thermodynamics
$\begin{aligned} W & =\Delta Q-\Delta U \\ & =Q-\frac{Q}{3}=\frac{2 Q}{3}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When temperature of an ideal gas is increased from $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $227^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, its rms speed is changed from $400 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ to $v_s$. Then, $v_s$ is
questions.solution:
We know that rms speed is directly proportional to square root of temperature
$\quad \qquad  v_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}$
Hence,$\frac{v_{\mathrm{rms}(1)}}{v_{\mathrm{rms}(2)}}=\sqrt{\frac{T_1}{T_2}}\begin{aligned} & \frac{400}{v_{\mathrm{rms}(2)}}=\frac{\sqrt{27+273}}{\sqrt{227+273}}=\sqrt{\frac{300}{500}} \\ & V_{\mathrm{rms}(2)}=\sqrt{\frac{500}{300}} \times 400 \\ & =1.29 \times 400=516.39 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \approx 516 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Equations of motion in the same direction are given by
$\begin{aligned}
& y_1=2 a \sin (\omega t-k x) \\
& y_2=2 a \sin (\omega t-k x-\theta)
\end{aligned}$
The amplitude of the medium particle will be
questions.solution:
The given equations of motion are
$\begin{aligned} & y_1=2 a \sin (\omega t-k x) \\ & y_2=2 a \sin (\omega t-k x-\theta)\end{aligned}$
Now the resultant equation of wave is given by
$\begin{aligned} & y=y_1+y_2 \\ & =2 a \sin (\omega t-k x)+2 a \sin (\omega t-k x-\theta) \\ & y=2 a\left[2 \sin \frac{(\omega t-k x+\omega t-k x-\theta)}{2}\times \cos \frac{\omega t-k x-(\omega t-k x-\theta)}{2}\right]\end{aligned}y=4 a \cos \frac{\theta}{2} \sin \left(\omega t-k x-\frac{\theta}{2}\right)$ ...(1)
Now comparing equation (1) with $y=A \sin (\omega t-k x)$, we have
Resultant amplitude $A=4 a \cos \frac{\theta}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A closed orgon pipe and an open orgon pipe are tuned to the same fundamental frequency. What is the ratio of their lengths?
questions.solution:
Avoiding end correction, the length of the closed organ pipe is
$l_1=\frac{\lambda_1}{4}$ or $\lambda_1=4 l_1$
The length of open organ pipe is
$l_2=\frac{\lambda_2}{2}$ or $\lambda_2=2 l_2$
Here, $n_1=n_2$
So, $\frac{v}{\lambda_1}=\frac{v}{\lambda_2}$ or $\frac{v}{4 l_1}=\frac{v}{2 l_2}$
Therefore, $l_1: l_2=1: 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a certain current is passed in the circuit as shown in figure, 10 kcal of heat is produced in $5 \Omega$ resistance. How much heat is produced in $4 \Omega$ resistance?
questions.solution:
Heat produced in $5 \Omega=10 \mathrm{kcal}$ Now from the relation. $H_1=i_1^2 R_1 t$ or $i_1^2=\frac{H_1}{R_1 t}$ or $\quad i_1^2=\frac{H_1}{5 t}$ ...(1) Again, $5 \times i_1=10 \times i_2$ or $i_2=\frac{i_1}{2}$
Now heat produced in $4 \Omega$ resistance is $\begin{aligned} H_2 & =i_2^2 R_2 t \\ i_2^2 & =\frac{H_2}{R_2 t}\end{aligned}$ or $\quad \frac{i_1^2}{4}=\frac{H_2}{4 t}$ or $i_1^2=\frac{H_2}{t}$ ...(2) From eqs. (1) and (2) $\begin{aligned} \frac{H_2}{t} & =\frac{H_1}{5 t} \\ \text { or } \quad H_2 & =\frac{H_1}{5}=\frac{10}{2}=2 \mathrm{kcal}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two similar coils are kept mutually perpendicular such that their centres coincide. At the centre, find the ratio of the magnetic field due to one coil and the resultant magnetic field through both coils, if the same current is flown.
questions.solution:
Suppose the magnetic field produced due to each coil is $B$.
The two coils are kept perpendicular hence, the angle between these is $90^{\circ}$ therefore, the resultant magnetic field is given by
$\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{B^2+B^2+2 B \cdot B \cdot \cos 90^{\circ}} \\ & =\sqrt{2 B^2+2 B^2 \times 0} \\ & =\sqrt{2 B^2}=B \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}$
Hence, the ratio of magnetic field due to one coil and the resultant magnetic field is given by
$=\frac{B}{\sqrt{2} B}=1: \sqrt{2}$

questions.q: An electron moves at right angle to a magnetic field of $1.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~T}$ with a speed of $6 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If the specific charge of the electron is $1.7 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{kg}$. The radius of the circular path will be
questions.solution:
The formula for radius of circular path is
$r=\frac{m v}{e B}=\frac{v}{\left(\frac{e}{m}\right) B}$ ...(1)
Given $: e / m$ of electron
$\begin{aligned}
& =1.7 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{kg} \text { and } v=6 \times 10^7 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
B & =1.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~T}
\end{aligned}\quad \begin{aligned} So, r & =\frac{6 \times 10^7}{1.7 \times 10^{11} \times 1.5 \times 10^{-2}} \\ & =2.35 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}=2.35 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A prism of refractive index $\sqrt{2}$ has a refracting angle of $60^{\circ}$. At what angle a ray must be incident on it so that it suffers a minimum deviation.
questions.solution:
The relation for refractive index of prism is
$\mu=\frac{\sin i}{\sin r}\ldots(1)$
The condition for minimum deviation is
$r=\frac{A}{2}=\frac{60^{\circ}}{2}=30^{\circ}$
Putting the given value of $\mu=\sqrt{2}$ and $r=30^{\circ}$ in eq (1), we get
$\begin{aligned} \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\sin i}{\sin 30^{\circ}} \\ \text { So, } \quad \sin i & =\sqrt{2} \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \sin i & =\sin 45^{\circ} \\ i & =45^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radius of the convex surface of planoconvex lens is 20 cm and the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5. The focal length is
questions.solution:
Using the relation for focal length of planoconvex lens
$=\frac{1}{f}=(\mu-1)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$
(Refractive index of material of lens $\mu=1.5$, $\left.R_1=20 \mathrm{~cm}, R_2=\infty\right)\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{f} & =(1.5-1)\left(\frac{1}{20}-\frac{1}{\infty}\right) \\ \frac{1}{f} & =\frac{1}{40} \\ \text { or } \quad f & =40 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A short linear object of length $b$ lies along the axis of a concave mirror of focal length $f$ at a distance $u$ from the pole of the mirror, what is the size of image?
questions.solution:
Using the relation for the focal length of concave mirror
$\frac{1}{f}=\frac{1}{v}+\frac{1}{u}$ ...(1)
Differentiating equation (1), we obtain
$0=-\frac{1}{v^2} d v-\frac{1}{u^2} d u$
So, $\quad d v=-\frac{v^2}{u^2} \times b\ldots(2)$
(Here : $d u=b$ )
From equation (1)
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{v} & =\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{u}=\frac{u-f}{f u} \\
\frac{u}{v} & =\frac{u-f}{f} \\
\end{aligned}\frac{v}{u}=\frac{f}{u-f}\ldots(3)$
Now, from equations (2) and (3), we get
$d v=-\left(\frac{f}{u-f}\right)^2 b$
Therefore, size or image is $=\left(\frac{f}{u-f}\right)^2 b$

questions.q: A person who can see things most clearly at a distance of 10 cm , requires spectacles to enable to see clearly things at a distance of 30 cm . What should be the focal length of the spectacles?

A concave lens is required by the person so that the lens forms the image of object distant 30 cm , at 10 cm it means

Hence, ratio of radii is 4

questions.solution: Decomposers are heterotropic organisms mostly bacteria and fungi which live on dead organic matter or detritus. They release different enzymes from their bodies into the dead and decaying plant and animal remains. The extra cellular digestion of the dead remains, lead to the release of simple inorganic substances.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Heparin is secreted by
questions.solution: Heparin is released from mast-cells. It is an anticoagulant which prevents activation of prothrombin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In frog chromosome number is reduced to half
questions.solution: Each primary oocyte undergo two maturation divisions, first meiotic and the second meiotic division. In the I-meiotic division, the primary oocyte divides into two unequal haploid daughter cells-a large secondary oocyte and very small first polar body. In II-maturation division, the first polar body may divide to form two second polar bodies. The secondary oocyte again divides into two unequal daughter cells, a large ootid and a very small second polar body. The ootid grows into a functional haploid ovum. The I meiotic division is reductional and II meiotic division is equational division.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one affects liver, muscle and adipose tissue?
questions.solution: Insulin affects liver, muscle and adipose tissue. In the muscular tissue it acts to promote carbohydrate metabolism and storage of glycogen. In liver cells, it favours glycongenesis, glycolysis and increases lipogenesis. In adipose tissue, in enhances the membrane transfer of glucose and promotes lipogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Secretion of gastric juice is stimulated by
questions.solution: The flow of gastric juice is regulated partly by a nervous mechanism and partly by the action of the hormone gastrin, which is produced in the mucosa cells of the stomach. It induces the secretion of gastric juice by gastric glands.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Deoxyribonuclease and ribonuclease are secreted by
questions.solution: eas. These enzymes act on DNA and RNA and convert them to deoxyribonucleotides and ribonucleotides, respectively. The optimum pH required by pancreatic juice to secrete these enzymes is $7-8$ (alkaline).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Disease caused by deficiency of protein in children is
questions.solution: Kwashiorkor is caused by the deficiency of proteins in diet. This disease occurs in children of age group 1 to 5 years. Its symptoms are oedema (swelling of abdomen), thining of limbs, diarrhoea and retarded brain.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the wall of alimentary canal, what is the actual sequence from outer to inner
options: serosa, long muscle, circular, submucosa, mucosa
questions.solution: The wall of alimentary canal is made up of four basic layers. Ist of all there is serosa which is a thin membranous covering around oesophagus. Then there is muscle layer-outer layer of longitudinal muscles and inner layer of circular muscles. Last there is submucosa, which contains a few oesophageal glands. Then comes mucosa, which have several layers of flattened cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Bile helps in the digestion of fat through
questions.solution: Bile contains no digestive enzymes, yet it plays an important role in fat digestion. It intensifies the 'mixing contractions' of intestinal wall. The organic salts by bile reduce the surface tension of fats globules and suspend them in water of digestive juice. It is emulsification of fats. It facilitates easy action of pancreatic juice on fats. They also help in formation of micelles which help to transport of all and products of fat digestion from intestinal lumen to absorptive cells. The inorganic bile salts import alkalinity to chyme and inactivate gastric pepsin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following represents the dental formula of man?
questions.solution: The number and kinds of teeth in a species of mammals can be represented by a sort of equation, which is called dental formula. The dental formula of $\operatorname{man}$ is $\frac{2 \cdot 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3}{2 \cdot 1 \cdot 2 \cdot 3}=32$.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one is antioxidant vitamin?
questions.solution: Three vitamins $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{E}$ and $\beta$-carotene (provitamin) are called antioxidant vitamin. Because they inactivate oxygen free radicals. Free radicals are highly reactive particles that carry an unpaired electron $\left[e^{-}\right]$, they damage cell membranes, DNA, other cellular structures and contribute to formation of artery narrowings and atherosclerosis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Nucleated RBC is present in
questions.solution: Nucleated RBCs are present in frog. In fishes, amphibians, reptiles and birds erythrocytes are usually nucleated, oval and biconvex, but in mammals they are non-nucleated and biconcave.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In diastole, heart is filled by
questions.solution: During joint diastole, blood continues to flow into auricle through the great viens (superior and inferior venae cavae), which bring venous blood from all parts of the body. During atrial diastole, venous blood again passes from the great veins to the auricle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Schwann cell is found around
questions.solution: All multicellular animals contain elongated nerve cells, called neurons. Each neuron has a cell body, axon and smaller processes called dendrites. An axon is the process of a nerve cell that carries impulses away from it. Axons run parallel to one another and each is surrounded along its whole length by series of Schwann cells. They may have myelin sheath.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which part of retina consists of only cones?
questions.solution: Lateral to the blind spot, there is a dipressed area of the retina, called fovea centralis, which contains only cones. Ability for vision is highest in the fovea.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Reflex action involves
questions.solution: Reflexes are classified as the spinal reflexes and the cranial reflexes. The former are so called because their basic neural path leads through spinal nerves and spinal cord. Reflexes at the spinal level have the purpose of removing the animal from harmful stimuli.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one is not correct?
questions.solution: The animals that excrete nitrogen in the form of urea are called ureotelic. Ureotelic animals include man and all other mammals and aquatic mammals like whales. So, whale is ureotelic and not ammonotelic.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The main excretory organ of prawn is
questions.solution: The main excretory organs of prawn are paired green glands. They are located within the second antennae, which are the second pair of appendages, attached to the anterior part of the body. Each green gland consists of an endsac, labyrinth and a bladder.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Haemodialysis helps in patient having
questions.solution: Haemodialysis helps the patient suffering from uremia. In this condition, the excretory products (i.e., urea) go on accumulating in blood. This happens due to kidney failure. In haemodialysis the patients blood is passed through disposable dialyser and is then returned to body by the intravenous route.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The thin filaments of a muscle fibre are made up of
questions.solution: oponin and tropomyosin. One thin filament probably contains 300-400 actin molecules, about 50 tropomyosin and 50 troponin. It is said that tropomyosin plays a vital role in sensitizing the contractile proteins (actin and myosin) to calcium ions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Progesterone is secreted by
questions.solution: Progesterone is a principle female sex hormone. It is a steroid. It is secreted during the later half of the menstrual cycle in human females by temporary endocrine tissue, the corpus luteum. The luteinizing hormone (LH) of anterior pituitary brings about a rupture of the Graafian folllicle to release the ovum and changes the ruptured follicle into a yellow structure called corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What's the difference between RNA and DNA?
questions.solution: DNA has deoxy ribose pentose sugar and four nitrogenous bases i.e. adenine [A], guanine [G], both are purines and cytosine $[\mathrm{C}]$, thymine $[\mathrm{T}]$ are pyrimidines. While RNA has ribose pentose sugar and four nitrogenous bases as in DNA except uracil [U] in place of thymine.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: DNA replication generally proceeds in a
questions.solution: DNA synthesis or replication always proceeds in $\mathrm{C}_5 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_3$ direction. Both the strands replicate by the addition of nucleotide monomer in $\mathrm{C}_5 \rightarrow \mathrm{C}_3$ direction.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Ischihara chart is used to detect
questions.solution: Ischihara chart is used to detect colourblindness.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The children of a haemophilic man and a normal woman are
options: neither sons nor daughters are haemophilic
questions.solution: The children of a haemophilic man and normal woman will be all normal. Neither sons nor daughters (only carrier) will be haemophilic.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If a plant having yellow or round seeds was crossed with another plant having green and wrinkled seeds then $F_1$ progeny are in the ratio
questions.solution: Mendel crossed a dominant homozygous yellow, round seeded plant with a recessive homozygous green and wrinkled seeded plant. The $\mathrm{F}_1$ offsprings produced are heterozygous yellow, round seeded plants parents : yellow round \times Green wrinkled.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: X-rays are used in
questions.solution: $X$-rays are used in CT-scan (computed tomographic scanning). It uses $X$-rays but employs a computer for reconstructing the image instead of directly recording it on a photographic film. This technique is used in the diagnosis of diseases of brain, spinal cord, chest, etc. It is also useful in detecting tumors.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Abnormal growth of the tumor in cancer is due to
questions.solution: Sometimes certain cells, which have differentiated and stopped dividing, suddenly start multiplying in an uncontrolled way to form a malignant growth called tumor. All cells carry certain cancer producing oncogenes. Under certain conditions these oncogenes are triggered to form masses of cells (tumor).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Antibody is produced by
questions.solution: -lymphocyte. Lymphocytes are critical for immune reactions and of two types B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes. B-lymphocytes, upon contact with appropriate antigens, are transformed into plasma cells, which are responsible for the production of antibody. They produce, 20 trillion antibodies per day.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one has no intermediate host?
questions.solution: Ascaris lumbricoides (the common roundworm) has no intermediate host. Man acquires infection by directly ingesting Ascaris eggs having the infective second stage-rhabditoid larva, with contaminated food or water.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q: The Triticale is an intergeneric hybrid between
questions.solution:
The Triticale is the first man made cereal. It is formed by a cross between wheat (Triticum) and rye (Secale cerale) followed by allopolyploidy (multiplication of none homologous chromosomes).
$\text{Triticum sp} \times \text{Secale cerale} \rightarrow \text{Diploid} \xrightarrow{\text{Allopolyploidy}} \text{Triticale}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following can help in the diagnosis of a genetical disorder?
questions.solution: PCR is a technique in which a small fragment of DNA is rapidly cloned or duplicated to produce multiple DNA copies. Thus, it helps in the diagnosis of a genetical disorder. This technique was conceived by American biochemist Kary B. Mullis.
